body:
FOUND WHILE FIXING T194, 2026-08-19, by staging §21.7 coexistence against a channel and watching one
of the two lenses simply not arrive.

bindArrived derives a manifest alias from the hyperschema ENTITY:

    hyperschema:Plant -> alias "Plant" -> living name "<prefix>:Plant"

So a peer publishing TWO lenses over ONE entity — which §21.7 explicitly supports, and which is how a
sibling reading exists at all — federates as ONE lens. The rail measured it: alice publishes lenses
"Plant" and "Sprout" both at hyperschema:Plant, and the receiver's sync reports bound: ["alice:Plant"]
only. "Sprout" is not parked, not refused, not mentioned. It is invisible.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THE MISSING LENS: this is H6 wearing a different hat. The alias, and therefore
the living name a reader asks by, is derived from the PROGRAM's address rather than from the READING.
Every consequence follows from that one substitution:
- a peer's sibling readings collapse into whichever one the entity scan reaches;
- the receiver cannot name them apart even if they wanted to, because the prefix scheme has one slot
  per entity;
- and T194's entity-vs-lens defects were unreachable through a channel only BECAUSE of this bug —
  the aliasing forces entity and lens to coincide. Fix this and those become reachable, which is why
  T194's fix was made properly rather than scoped to what is reachable today.

THE SHAPE THAT LOOKS RIGHT (not decided): enumerate the pool's registration bindings by their LENS
name (the `schema` pointer's target, minus the `schema:` prefix — the same read T194's fix now uses),
mint one manifest row per lens rather than per entity, and let the living name be
`<prefix>:<lensName>`. Two rows may then share a target entity, which is what a manifest is for.

RAILS:
1. A peer with two lenses at one hyperschema entity federates as TWO bound names.
2. Two-sided: a peer with one lens at one entity still binds exactly one, under the same name as
   today — no existing channel changes its surface.
3. Cursing one sibling leaves the other serving (this is T194's rail, which cannot run until this
   lands — it is currently restaged onto a weaker corpus and says so).

TIER: self-merge. It widens what federates rather than what is purged, and it repairs a promise §21.7
already makes.
title: A peer's sibling lenses at one hyperschema entity federate as one — the alias is entity-derived
